findings.title: The last-rename-wins residual is real, durable and gate-reddening; it deserves a follow-up ticket (this diff correctly leaves it)
findings.evidence: mergeTaskMeta reads at spool.mjs:212 and writes at :217; the belt calls it per row at reconciler-documents.mjs:267 with a DB snapshot that carries NO transport (documentTaskSnapshot, :199-228, selects task columns only). Hand-interleaved probe on the POST-fix code (belt read before intake.mjs:439, belt write after intake.mjs:442), Windows and Linux/WSL, both: {"beltBase":null,"storageKeyAfter":null,"sha256After":null,"runIdAfter":null} -- the transport is gone and no later sweep restores it, because every subsequent merge base is the transport-less body and the runtime holds no SELECT on clara.documents (PIN-AB-6). Blast radius is the SAME visible failure the splice produced: documentIngest.behavior_v2.mjs:190 hands task.storageKey to downloadCanonical and storage.mjs:35 throws StorageError('storage_error','canonical storage key is invalid') -- the exact FatalError in the implementer's pre-fix loop logs (loop-prefix/3.leg1.log:43, 5.leg2.log:102). If the run is not yet enqueued the belt instead refuses to dispatch at reconciler-documents.mjs:409-413. The window is much narrower than the fixed defect: intake writes the full sidecar twice (intake.mjs:439, then :442 after enqueue), so a stale belt write landing between them is REPAIRED by :442; only a belt read preceding :439 whose write lands after :442 loses the transport, i.e. the belt's read-write gap must straddle the whole enqueue round trip. That is why it is not what reddened CI twice in a row.
findings.fix: File a follow-up ticket for a version/mtime compare-and-swap (or a per-task lock) across spool.mjs's writers, as mergeTaskMeta's own header (documentIngest task #28, P4) already anticipates. No change to this diff.

findings.title: The uuid temp name spends 23 characters of Windows MAX_PATH headroom
findings.evidence: task-<uuid>.json.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp is 23 characters longer than task-<uuid>.json.<pid>.<ms>.tmp. With a spool root of the shape this session actually uses (159 chars, the per-session scratchpad temp dir) the temp path goes 230 -> 253 of the 260-char Windows limit; measured, not assumed. CI is Linux (255-BYTE filename limit, filename here about 100 bytes), so it cannot red the gate, and the 17-cell file passes on this rig under a 159-char root (node --test tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs: 17 pass, 0 fail).
findings.fix: If a Windows ENAMETOOLONG ever appears, a process-local counter (${path}.${pid}.${seq++}.tmp) is strictly unique per call in-process while pid keeps cross-process uniqueness, at a fraction of the length. Not worth changing now.

findings.title: The ticket's second desired behaviour is answered by falsifying its premise, not delivered as isolation
findings.evidence: The ticket asks that 'a leg cannot fail because of what an earlier leg queued or removed'. The verified diagnosis is that no leg removed anything: the ENOENT is the temp file, not the spool directory (spool.mjs:140 against the CI path .../spool/task-<id>.json.7113.1790191021685.tmp), and the #967 AC3 throw was truthful -- the run genuinely failed under that leg's own engine. The legs still share one database and one CLARA_SPOOL_DIR by design (.github/actions/db-live-gates/action.yml:99-137, both legs on clara_intake_ci), so cross-leg coupling is structurally unchanged.
findings.fix: Nothing to change; the report already says this. Worth one line in the PR body so the closer does not read the ticket's premise as an unmet acceptance criterion.

answers.q1: Confirmed on all three points. (a) Same-process, same-millisecond collision was possible on the CI path: both writers live in ONE process -- the standalone driver imports the built server in-process (tests/intake-admission-e2e.mjs:352, await import('../.output/server/index.mjs')), whose startWorld plugin runs the reconciler leader loop (plugins/startWorld.ts:30 and :345), and the CI log shows [reconcile] sweep lines and the runtime's own intake FAILED lines inside one step (job 107339673336 lines 1944-1952; 'LEADER acquired' at 19:17:01.62 immediately before the ENOENT at 19:17:01.689). The two writers are intake.mjs:439 (writeTaskMeta of the full transport task before enqueue, :442 again after) and reconciler-documents.mjs:267 (mergeTaskMeta of every clara.document_processing_tasks row, every sweep); the DB row is committed by clara.finalize_document_intake before :439 runs, so the belt can see the task before its sidecar exists. (b) The fix removes it: the temp name's per-call component is now randomUUID() (spool.mjs:140), so no two calls in one process can share an inode. Independent probe of the two real writer shapes, 300 rounds, pre-fix against post-fix -- Linux/WSL (the CI shape) 291 ENOENT and 277 unparseable -> 0 and 0; Windows 0 ENOENT and 92 unparseable -> 0 and 0. Both names still end in .tmp, so SPOOL_REAPABLE (spool.mjs:478, requires .bin or .json) and listJsonEntries (:299, requires .json) ignore them exactly as before. (c) The retry set is contention-only and excludes ENOENT: const RENAME_CONTENDED = new Set(["EPERM", "EACCES", "EBUSY"]) at spool.mjs:55, consulted at :101 -- if (!RENAME_CONTENDED.has(err?.code) || Date.now() >= deadline) throw err.
answers.q2: Fails pre-fix, passes post-fix, and it is a real reproduction rather than a tautology. Post-fix, tree untouched: node --test --test-name-pattern p1043 tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs -> '# pass 1' in 2.58 s. Pre-fix WITHOUT modifying the worktree: a resolve hook (scratchpad register.mjs plus hooks.mjs) redirected every lib/spool.mjs specifier to 'git show 67f70ea0f:packages/runtime/lib/spool.mjs' saved in the scratchpad; the same command gave 'not ok 1 ... no writer may be told its write failed because a sibling in the SAME process won the race: 1 of 400 writes threw ([{"round":19,"code":"ENOENT"}])' at tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs:279. The worktree was never edited (git status --porcelain empty before and after; a single transient staged packages/db/tests/__check857_selftest_decoy.mjs seen at 03:57 belongs to another agent working in the same worktree and cleared itself). The cell is genuine: it drives two DIFFERENT real bodies (the full transport sidecar of intake.mjs:439 and the shorter DB-row merge of reconciler-documents.mjs:267) concurrently through Promise.allSettled against ONE task sidecar, asserts the body on disk equals one of them field for field rather than merely parsing, and asserts both writers won rounds. My own 300-round probe of the same shape recorded wins {intake:107, reconciler:101} pre-fix and {intake:119, reconciler:181} post-fix, so both sides really do land. Windows is the thin host (1 of 400 writes threw); Linux, the runner's platform, is where the margin is wide (291 of 600).
answers.q3: Confirmed: the two 'not found' lines are a PASSING leg's own token-lock control, not a defect. From gh run view --job 107339673336 --log: the Slice-5 intake transport e2e step starts at 19:13:51.416 (line 687), the two lines are at 19:16:56.155 and 19:16:56.160 for intake ids 66a4b21e and 05ef5523 (lines 1951-1952), that step prints INTAKE E2E: PASS at 19:16:59.808 and [world-gate] ... exit 0 (lines 1961-1962), and the admission step only begins at 19:16:59.878 (line 1964). The source is tests/intake-e2e.mjs:190-201 -- two finalize calls with authorization 'Bearer wrong', one on the real intake id and one on a random uuid, both asserted 404 -- which hit requireCapability (intake.mjs:113-116: readIntakeMeta(...).catch(() => null), then IntakeError(404,'not_found','not found')). finalizeDocumentIntake's catch logs every failure, failureCode (intake.mjs:154-159) folds not_found to internal because it is not in the allow-list, and canonicalReached is false because meta was never assigned (intake.mjs:294-301). The ticket's third line (19:17:01.689, canonicalReached=true, ENOENT on the .7113.1790191021685.tmp rename) is the real defect, 1.8 s into the admission step and one line before its FAIL.
answers.q4: The lost update is real, durable and can red the gate, so the follow-up is worth filing (finding S1). Mechanically: mergeTaskMeta reads at spool.mjs:212 and writes at :217, and the belt's patch carries no transport (documentTaskSnapshot, reconciler-documents.mjs:199-228), so a merge whose base was read before intake.mjs:439 and whose write lands after intake.mjs:442 leaves a sidecar with no storageKey and no sha256 -- reproduced by hand-interleaving against the POST-fix code on both platforms ({"storageKeyAfter":null,"sha256After":null,"runIdAfter":null}). It is durable: later sweeps merge onto the damaged body, and the runtime cannot recover the key from clara.documents (PIN-AB-6), so only a re-upload's 0051 section 2 echo restores it. It shows exactly as the report says -- '[reconcile] ingest task ... has no transport metadata in its sidecar -- NOT dispatched' (reconciler-documents.mjs:411) with NO preceding 'task sidecar unreadable' line; if the run was already enqueued at intake.mjs:442 the workflow instead reads the stripped sidecar (documentIngest.behavior_v2.mjs:176 and :190) and manufactures storage_error 'canonical storage key is invalid' (storage.mjs:35), the same FatalError the pre-fix loop logs carry. Frequency is far below the fixed defect's, because intake's second write repairs any belt write landing between :439 and :442, so the damaging case needs the belt's read-write gap to straddle the enqueue round trip. Follow-up ticket, not a blocker, and the report's residual paragraph is accurate as written.
answers.q5: Benign as claimed, and now measured rather than judged. The probe is .ready-${process.pid}-${Date.now()} (spool.mjs:457), written with the same two-byte body 'ok' and removed with rm(probe, {force:true}) (:459), so two probes in one millisecond can only write identical content into one inode and then remove a file the sibling may already have removed, which force:true swallows; there is no rename to lose and no body to splice. 600 concurrent probes (200 rounds of three) against the post-fix module gave Windows {notOk:0, threw:0, leftovers:[]} and Linux/WSL {notOk:0, threw:0, leftovers:[]}, identical on the pre-fix module. Worth knowing but not acting on: a .ready- file orphaned by a crash matches neither SPOOL_REAPABLE (spool.mjs:478) nor listJsonEntries (:299) and would never be swept -- pre-existing, untouched by this diff, two bytes.
answers.q6: Nothing extra, and nothing the ticket asks for is missing except the criterion that cannot exist yet. The diff is three files: the one-line fix and its header (packages/runtime/lib/spool.mjs, plus one import symbol), the regression cell and its three new imports (tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs), and a README defect entry in that file's existing house style (the #966 and #981 entries sit around it). No product code outside atomicJson, no timeout widened, no retry added, no sleep. Criterion by criterion: the feedback loop is recorded (scratchpad loop-1043.sh), and the deterministic two-second unit probe probe-atomic.mjs is timestamped 03:27:02, BEFORE the fix commit 1ecf1f3d9 at 03:30:57 -- the five-minute composite loop's pre-fix red was measured at 03:33-03:39 against a reverted spool.mjs with a rebuilt bundle, which is code-equivalent to the pre-fix tree, so the criterion is met in substance. The root cause is named at the seam and fixed there, and the regression cell is red then green (q2). The five-green criterion I verified rather than trusted: loop-postfix holds six cycles times two legs, every one INTAKE E2E: PASS and INTAKE ADMISSION E2E: PASS (03:39:56 to 03:42:16), each cycle preceded by its own DROP DATABASE, CREATE DATABASE and bootstrap in n.provision.log, all after the bundle rebuild at 03:39:47, and the built bundle carries the fix (the randomUUID temp name is present in packages/runtime/.output/server/index.mjs). loop-prefix shows exactly the two claimed reds: 3.leg1 with 'task sidecar unreadable ... position 737' then storage_error, and 5.leg2 with the #967 AC3 throw. I re-ran the whole touched test file: 17 pass, 0 fail. The final criterion (CI green on the fix PR including db-live-gates) is open because no PR exists, which the task states is expected and the report also flags. I did not re-run pnpm lint or the six-file unit battery; those are the Standards axis's ground and the report's claims there are unverified by me.
